title: Windows relay login lifecycle
summary: The native Windows relay uses an interactive per-user scheduled task that runs the relay runtime's pythonw.exe, so no console window opens: the task runner has no stdio and writes its own messages and crashes to the relay's stderr log, and it starts the relay with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and its output in the relay's log files. The runner restarts the relay on every exit, after 2 seconds and backing off to 60 seconds while it keeps exiting quickly, until the task is ended; Task Scheduler's RestartOnFailure covers only a task that fails to launch. Sign-out stops it; reboot leaves it unavailable before login; the next login starts it. Desktop lock leaves it running. Battery use does not stop it. Task Scheduler restrictions report the reason and recovery. There is no guaranteed shutdown grace period; durable custody is reconciled at the next start. Setup installs the task for local and HTTPS destinations; a local-universe task runs the installer's yoke.cmd shim or an environment's yoke.exe. Ending or removing the task also stops the relay it started. Relay status shows its identity, enabled state and policy refusal, and an outdated task names each setting that differs; settings Task Scheduler omits because they hold their default, or a user exported by name instead of SID, still match. yoke update and yoke project refresh run the updated CLI's relay status for each configured environment and reinstall an installed task that no longer matches, such as one still running python.exe; a failed reinstall fails the command with its recovery. yoke status reports relay_down, an error that clears ok, without importing the engine: when no relay process runs from a release-following relay's state directory (the task runner alone does not count), or the control plane has a relay of this machine but no current heartbeat from it; it names the task runner's restart and yoke relay install. Doctor's session-relay check reads the same task on native Windows and fails, naming each, when it is missing, outdated, disabled or not running; heartbeat and credential checks match macOS and Linux. Windows lab proof is owed after deploy.
